name: Alkylation (HF, sulfuric, ionic liquid, solid acid)
applications: high-octane, low-vapour-pressure gasoline blendstock from FCC olefins
principle: Isobutane reacts with light olefins (propylene, butylenes) over a strong acid catalyst to make branched paraffins called alkylate. Conventional units use hydrofluoric or sulfuric acid; newer units use ionic liquids or solid acids to remove the hazards of HF or the cost of acid regeneration.

process_steps.name: Reaction
equipment: reactor (contactor, settler or ionic liquid reactor)

reference_plants.name: Chevron Salt Lake City refinery ISOALKY unit
reference_plants.capacity: retrofit of a 4,500 b/d HF alkylation unit in a 58,000 b/d refinery, with capacity increased
reference_plants.status: first commercial ionic liquid alkylation; start-up announced 13 April 2021

advantages: Alkylate is a clean, high-octane blendstock
Ionic liquid and solid acid routes avoid HF hazards
limitations: HF is highly toxic; sulfuric needs acid regeneration
